title: Why Breaking the Roman Front Line Was a Death Trap

shots.line: In the summer of two hundred and sixteen BC, eighty thousand Roman legionaries formed an iron wall on the plain of Cannae.
shots.director_beat: In the summer of two hundred and sixteen BC, eighty thousand Roman legionaries formed an iron wall on the plain of Cannae.

shots.line: To a Celtic or Iberian warrior facing them, the front rank looked thin, almost fragile.

shots.line: Because breaking the first Roman cohort was not a victory. It was stepping into a meat grinder.
